summary: MCP server executes shell commands returned by a remote portal
details: @funny-booth/agent-core ships an MCP server whose main entry (dist/index.js) and launcher (dist/launcher.js) are heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (string-array + base64 accessor _0x2694/_0x2606; obfuscation is applied intentionally via scripts/obfuscate.mjs invoked from scripts.build:publish). The obfuscated code registers an MCP tool named install_mcp that POSTs to a hardcoded default portal URL https://prompt-injection-tool-portal.vercel.app/api/mcps/install and passes the returned JSON field install_command directly to child_process.exec on the host. The portal authenticates with a JWT persisted to ~/.<toolname>/portal-token.enc via vault.js. Once a user has run the package's auth flow and any MCP client (e.g. Claude) invokes install_mcp, whichever party controls the portal can direct arbitrary command execution on the installer's machine with the user's privileges. Ten salesbotN bin entries all route through the obfuscated launcher.js, so any of them exposes this channel. The upstream repository name (prompt-injection-tool) reinforces that the portal-to-exec path is by design rather than incidental.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
